thread:
emily: Heads up \/– Customer 'Beacon' asked for a paid surge protection product: "guaranteed" baseline throughput + prepaid surge tokens for unpredictable spikes. Procurement wants a packaging option fast. @tom @juan can you weigh in?

tom: Are they asking for geographic reservations or just prioritized queuing? we need to narrow scope for beta.

emily: Sales says EU latency and US-East launch spikes are the main concerns. They don't need full Dedicated infra if we can promise a practical guardrail for launches.

juan: Technical take: we can do prioritized routing + a regional reservation flag without full Dedicated if we combine token-bucket burst tokens with per-customer priority weight. Work: routing config, credit ledger, billing hook, plus telemetry. Roughly 4 weeks for MVP if we limit to hosted-only.

nina: From pricing ops: recommend two SKUs: 1) SurgeGuard Baseline (monthly reserve) 2) SurgeTokens (prepaid packs). Baseline covers reserved QPS and reserved billing line; tokens consumed during spikes.

peter: Legal: using "guaranteed" in marketing triggers SLA implications. Suggest "Priority-assisted throughput" in the product language and a short SLA addendum only for Dedicated. For hosted + tokens we can do a softer SLO and credits limited to 3% of monthly fees.

emily: Quick draft packaging options for discussion:
```
- SurgeGuard - Hosted Baseline: $75k/mo reserve -> up to 1,200 reserved QPS, soft SLO for latency, no regional exclusivity.
- SurgeTokens: prepay packs ($10k = 100k token-usage-equivalent) consumed only when baseline exceeded.
- SurgeGuard - Regional Dedicated: $350k/mo regional pool, SLA (p99 latency), includes 20% burst buffer and priority routing.
```

juan: Implementation detail: ledger service needs an atomic check-and-debit on token usage; routing must consult customer balance in <10ms path. Suggest caching balance at edge for 1s and fallback to permissive mode on RPC failure.

tom: Sales ask: can we guarantee 30% burst without extra negotiation? If we sell SurgeTokens as prepaid packs that should cover it. We should have a maximum allowed burst multiplier per month to protect capacity.

nina: Suggested commercial guardrails: minimum beta commit = $75k/mo for 3 months OR $50k/mo + $25k prepaid tokens. Beta customers get waived setup fee.

peter: Contract clause idea: "Customer's SurgeGuard entitlement is subject to Service Limits; Hosted SurgeGuard provides prioritized ingress but does not provide exclusive compute capacity. Exclusive regional capacity requires Regional Dedicated purchase." I'll draft redlines.

emily: Launch criteria (must-have before private beta):
- Routing flag + edge cache for token balance (canary)
- Billing integration: token purchase + consumption on invoice line
- Dashboards: reserved vs token consumption, failover counts
- Legal: token terms, SLO language for hosted baseline
- Support: incident runbook and escalation path

If we hit these we can onboard 1-2 anchor customers for 6-week beta.

juan: Timeline: if we scope to hosted-only + tokens, 4 weeks for infra + 1 week for billing + 1 week for ops/runbooks = 6 weeks. Dedicated not included.

tom: Pricing example for Beacon to model in procurement deck (placeholder):
```
baseline commit: $80,000/mo -> 1,250 reserved QPS
prepaid tokens: $30,000 pack -> covers ~250k token-usage-equivalent
burst overage: when tokens exhausted -> charged at 1.5x list per-token rate
beta discount: 10% off baseline for first 3 months
```

billing-bot: invoice line template created: "SurgeGuard Baseline (region)" + "SurgeTokens (pack)".

emily: Ops ask: set a hard cap on allowed burst multiplier (we'll define per customer) and surface alerts when tokens drop <20%.

juan: Engineering action items: build token ledger PR, add routing flag, expose metrics. ETA: first PR end of week 1.

peter: I'll produce SLA language & short addendum by Wed EOD.

nina: I'll map token SKUs to billing product codes and propose invoice format by Thu.

emily: OK good rhythm. I'll schedule gating review in 8 days. If sales wants to show procurement earlier, they should use the pricing placeholders only. :+1:
